title: Generator manifest (generator.json)
description: Describes one model generator so Generator Library can list, install, launch and update it.

id.description: Stable, unique, lowercase. Changing it makes the library treat the generator as new.

version.description: Informational; the library tracks release tags and commits for updates.

summary.description: One sentence shown on the card.

description.description: Longer text shown in the detail view. Newlines are kept.

process.description: What the output is for: 3d-print, laser, cnc, tool…

icon.description: Path in the repository, or an https URL.

repo.description: owner/name on GitHub. Defaults to the repository the manifest was read from.

upstream.description: For forks: the original repository, shown as a link.

repo.description: Release repository when it differs from the manifest's repo (for example the upstream of a fork).

tag.description: "latest", an exact tag, or a glob such as desktop-v*.

asset.description: Asset file name or glob, e.g. Terrain-Press-*-Portable.exe

ref.description: Branch or tag; default branch when omitted.

path.description: Folder inside the repository to install, e.g. site or dist. Empty means the whole tree.

url.description: web and mirror: the page to open or capture.

githubPagesFiles.description: mirror: also pull every published repository file (WebMirror's GitHub Pages mode).

browserCapture.description: mirror: capture JavaScript-loaded assets with a local Chrome/Edge.

from.description: bundle and exe: where the files come from.

entry.description: bundle: page to open, relative to the unpacked folder.

spa.description: bundle: serve the entry page for unknown routes (client-side routing).

install.description: exe: portable runs the file; installer runs it once to install; zip unpacks and runs exec.

exec.description: exe: executable path inside the unpacked archive (zip) or the file the installer leaves behind.
